0:00 / 1:52

0:00 Intro. Terminal windows pile up faster and faster until the screen is buried, one per agent, each waiting on a person: an edit to approve, a plan to review, a conflict to resolve. It starts with one agent. Then five. Then a dozen. Every one of them is waiting on you. Keeping them all moving becomes your full-time job. Loupe lets you focus on the important stuff.

The example project is Driftwood, a made-up cabin-rental site.

0:10 The board. On the Driftwood board, card #42 “Show the nightly price on search cards” sits in Backlog. It is dragged to Product design.

0:14 Product design. The bridge opens a terminal with Claude Code running /loupe:product-design 42. Where the price sits on the card is a look-and-feel choice, so Claude offers a Design canvas and builds two mockups: a price badge on the photo, and a price line under the name. On the canvas the owner comments on option 1: show the total for the dates too. Claude reads the comment back, confirms the pick, writes the product document and links it to the card.

0:35 You review. The document opens rendered. The reviewer selects the R2 sentence, comments that no scenario covers a search with no dates, and finishes the review with Request changes and a note.

0:53 The agent revises. The loupe bridge runs a fix-round worker. Version 2 adds a scenario for a search with no dates and answers the comment. The reviewer approves it.

1:05 The build. The approval moves the card to Tech design, where a worker writes the tech design. After its approval, an implementation worker builds the change, opens pull request 641 and moves the card to In review.

1:14 Agent review. On GitHub, the Loupe agent review approves pull request 641.

1:16 Site review. On the preview of pull request 641, the reviewer opens the Review widget, picks a price badge and notes that it covers the Guest favourite label. The note lands on card #42 as feedback, and a fix worker moves the badge to the bottom of the photo.

1:29 Merge. The checks pass and the agent review approves the fix, so Loupe merges it on its own, and card #42 moves to Done by itself.

1:34 Shipped. On driftwood.cabins, every search card shows its price, and the Guest favourite label stays visible.

1:43 Loupe, the control plane for your agent loop.
